nodes.label: Activity Theory

properties.description: CHAT / Cultural-Historical Activity Theory — Engeström's expansive learning model frames human activity as mediated by tools and social context.

nodes.label: Science and Technology Studies (STS)

properties.description: Sociological lens examining how science and technology are socially constructed and how they shape society.

nodes.label: Value-Sensitive Design (VSD)

properties.description: Friedman & Hendry's design methodology that embeds human values into technical systems design.

nodes.label: Labor Process Theory

properties.description: Braverman-derived framework analyzing how capitalism shapes work, skill, and control in the labor process.

nodes.label: Sociotechnical Systems Theory

properties.description: Framework treating technology and social organization as co-evolving, interdependent systems.

nodes.label: Constructivism

properties.description: Learning theory holding that knowledge is actively constructed by learners through experience and social interaction.

nodes.label: Constructionism

properties.description: Papert's learning-by-making framework emphasizing knowledge construction through creation of shareable artifacts.

nodes.label: Reflective Practice

properties.description: Schön's framework of reflection-in-action and reflection-on-action as the epistemology of professional practice.

nodes.label: Design Cognition

properties.description: Research tradition studying how designers think, frame problems, and generate solutions.

nodes.label: Job Crafting Theory

properties.description: Wrzesniewski & Dutton's model of how workers proactively reshape their job tasks, relationships, and identity.

nodes.label: Genealogical / Policy Analysis

properties.description: Foucauldian genealogy and policy assemblage analysis tracing how discourses construct social problems.

nodes.label: Sociotechnical Imaginaries

properties.description: Jasanoff's concept of collectively held visions of desirable futures co-produced by science, technology, and social order.

nodes.label: Cognitive Load Theory

properties.description: Sweller's theory of working memory limits and instructional design implications for multimedia learning.

nodes.label: Research through Design

properties.description: RtD epistemological framework treating design practice itself as a form of knowledge production.

nodes.label: Task-Based Model of Automation

properties.description: Autor et al.'s framework decomposing jobs into routine/non-routine tasks to analyze automation's labor market effects.

nodes.label: Participatory Design Theory

properties.description: Scandinavian tradition of involving users and stakeholders as co-designers throughout the design process.

nodes.label: Sensemaking Theory

properties.description: Weick's organizational theory of how actors construct meaning from ambiguous situations.

nodes.label: Critical Theory / Political Economy

properties.description: Tradition examining how power, capital, and ideology shape technology development and its social effects.

nodes.label: AI Literacy Framework

properties.description: Long & Magerko's multidimensional framework for understanding and teaching AI competencies.

nodes.label: Information Processing Theory

properties.description: Cognitive model of learning based on attention, encoding, and retrieval in working and long-term memory.

nodes.label: Human Performance Technology (HPT)

properties.description: Gilbert's Behavior Engineering Model and systems-based approach to performance improvement.

nodes.label: Organizational Learning Theory

properties.description: March's exploitation/exploration framework and related theories of how organizations adapt and learn.

nodes.label: User-Centered Design

properties.description: ISO 9241-210 / Norman's HCD process — iterates research, design, and evaluation to optimize usability and user experience.

nodes.label: Design Thinking

properties.description: IDEO/d.school's human-centered innovation process: empathize, define, ideate, prototype, test.

nodes.label: Technology Acceptance Model

properties.description: Davis's model of perceived usefulness and ease-of-use as determinants of technology adoption behavior.

nodes.label: Ironies of Automation

properties.description: Bainbridge's theory that automation transfers difficult cognitive work to humans, increasing the cost of human error.

nodes.label: Cooperative Learning Theory

properties.description: Johnson & Johnson / Slavin's framework of structured interdependence and group accountability in learning.

nodes.label: Cybernetics

properties.description: Wiener's theory of control and communication in animals and machines; foundational to human-computer systems thinking.

nodes.label: Posthumanism

properties.description: Haraway/Barad's framework dissolving human/machine boundaries in favor of material-discursive entanglement.

nodes.label: Job Characteristics Theory

properties.description: Hackman & Oldham's model of how core job dimensions (skill variety, autonomy, feedback) shape motivation and satisfaction.

nodes.label: Semi-Structured Interviews

properties.description: Qualitative data collection through open-ended guided conversations with participants.

nodes.label: Thematic Analysis

properties.description: Qualitative analysis identifying, coding, and interpreting patterns of meaning across a dataset.

nodes.label: Systematic Literature Review

properties.description: Structured, reproducible search and synthesis of published research using explicit inclusion criteria.

nodes.label: Survey / Questionnaire Study

properties.description: Structured data collection from a sample using standardized self-report instruments.

nodes.label: Historical Analysis

properties.description: Examination of primary and archival sources to trace development of ideas, practices, or events over time.

nodes.label: Case Study

properties.description: In-depth investigation of a bounded instance (person, organization, project) to develop theoretical understanding.

nodes.label: Conceptual / Theoretical Analysis

properties.description: Development or critique of theoretical frameworks without primary empirical data collection.

nodes.label: Ethnography

properties.description: Extended immersive fieldwork combining observation and interviews to understand situated practice.

nodes.label: Mixed Methods

properties.description: Research design combining quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis.

nodes.label: Discourse Analysis

properties.description: Examination of language use in texts and talk to reveal how meaning and power are constructed.

nodes.label: Participatory Design Sessions

properties.description: Co-design workshops or sessions where users/stakeholders actively shape design outcomes.

nodes.label: Design-Based Research

properties.description: Iterative research methodology integrating design, implementation, and analysis in authentic settings.

nodes.label: Protocol Analysis

properties.description: Verbal think-aloud or behavioral trace methods for studying cognitive processes in real time.

nodes.label: Wizard-of-Oz Study

properties.description: Research technique simulating system capabilities with a hidden human operator to study user interaction.

nodes.label: Quantitative / Statistical Analysis

properties.description: Analysis of numerical data using statistical methods including regression, panel data, and experimental designs.

nodes.label: Action Research

properties.description: Practitioner-led inquiry cycles of planning, acting, observing, and reflecting in real educational/professional settings.

nodes.label: Bibliometric Analysis

properties.description: Quantitative mapping of scholarly literature through citation counts, co-citation networks, and keyword co-occurrence.

nodes.label: Diary Study

properties.description: Longitudinal self-report method where participants log experiences, behaviors, or tool use over days or weeks.

nodes.label: Narrative Review

properties.description: Non-systematic synthesis that interprets and narrates a body of literature without exhaustive database search protocols.

nodes.label: Formative Usability Study

properties.description: Early-stage user testing to identify design problems before deployment, often with think-aloud or structured observation.

nodes.label: Phenomenography

properties.description: Qualitative methodology studying the qualitatively distinct ways different people experience or conceptualize a phenomenon.
